html:
The Munsee are the northern branch of the Lenape, an Algonquian people whose homeland was the lower Hudson Valley, northern New Jersey and the upper Delaware River. They spoke Munsee, one of the two Lenape languages.

The Lenape of Manhattan, who dealt with the Dutch of New Netherland in the 1620s, were Munsee speakers. Over the next century war, land sales, debts and epidemics pushed them west and north. Some joined the Lenape who moved to Ohio and later to Oklahoma; others went to Ontario, where the Munsee-Delaware Nation lives today; others merged with the Mahican as the Stockbridge-Munsee Community of Wisconsin. Their northern neighbours were the Haudenosaunee, with whom relations swung between alliance and conflict.
